description.narrative: The Sustaining Education and Learning (SEAL) Project, with Additional Financing from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), builds on the achievements of the Restoring Education and Learning (REAL) Emergency Project to protect and strengthen basic education in Yemen amid ongoing conflict and fragility. The project's overall objective is to strengthen Yemen's capacity to sustain basic education and learning in targeted schools, while preventing further erosion of human capital.The project combines school-level investments with system-strengthening interventions to improve both access and learning outcomes. It supports the rehabilitation of deteriorated classrooms, construction of new classrooms to reduce overcrowding, and provision of gender-sensitive water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) facilities. Targeted schools receive school grants to sustain operations, strengthen community engagement, and improve learning environments, with school selection guided by a Project Targeting Index and strict Entry Criteria of Access (ECA) to ensure feasibility in the highly fragile operating context.With the Additional Financing, the project expands its focus from access alone to foundational learning and instructional quality. New activities include the large-scale provision of textbooks and learning materials, structured student assessments, and remedial learning programs for children who have not acquired basic skills. Teachers, school principals, and supervisors receive intensive training, coaching, and digital supervision tools to strengthen classroom practice, school leadership, and performance monitoring. The project also places strong emphasis on girls education, including targeted support for Rural Female Teachers (RFTs) and measures to improve girls enrollment, retention, and safety in remote areas.Through this integrated approach, SEAL aims to sustain access, improve foundational learning, advance gender equity, and reinforce education system resilience, helping Yemen's children remain on track for learning and future productivity despite protracted conflict.
